Digital Epidemiology Workshop
Hands on exercise using web-based tools (EpiCollect, Pathogenwatch, Data-flo, Microreact) to conduct a genomic epidemiology investigation.
Centre for Genomic Pathogen Surveillance


Infectious Disease Genomic Epidemiology 2023
This 4-day course from CBW provides an introduction to genomic epidemiology analysis followed by hands-on practical tutorials demonstrating the use of selected analysis tools. The tutorials are designed as self-contained units that include example data and detailed instructions for installation of all required bioinformatics tools or access to publicly available web applications.
Bioinformatics.ca


Whole genome multi locus sequence typing activity
This activity was developed by the New York Integrated Food Safety Center of Excellence to provide public health staff or students of public health with an understanding of how whole genome sequencing (WGS), and particularly whole genome multi locus sequence typing (wgMLST), works as a subtyping method. The activity can be taken individually or in group (3-5 people per group suggested).
New York Food Safety Center of Excellence/ Cornell University


Bioinformatics for Genomic Epidemiology March 2024
An introductory course on Pathogen Bioinformatics for Genomic Epidemiology. Topics covered include Introduction Unix/Linux, command line, shell scripting, containers, Galaxy, Nextflow, R, and a cholera case study.

title: Making learning about antimicrobial resistance fun
text:
Now available as a printable version!



To get started, you’ll need to print out the game board and pieces:

Board and Pieces
Cards

You’ll also need to print out notes sheets, they print out two per page, and each player will need one

Player notes sheets

Don’t forget to print out the instructions!

Pathogen Pursuit Rules











Original handmade version of Pathogen Pursuit (someday I hope to have more available!)


Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a global concern, and one of the challenges of raising awareness is the complexity of the problem. There are so many different pathogens and resistance mechanisms!
Enter, games! Games are a great way to introduce complex topics in a fun and engaging way.
Pathogen Pursuit: A Hospital Whodunit is played like a detective game, but instead of solving a crime, players race to solve an outbreak in a hospital! The game features different Carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales (CPE) and an intrepid outbreak investigation team. Players will learn about different bacterial species often associated with hospital-acquired infections as well as different carbapenemenases that are contributing to the global crisis of antimicrobial resistance.


Have you played pathogen pursuit? I’d love your feedback! Submit it below.



The making of Pathogen Pursuit: A Hospital Whodunit
One of my hobbies is designing and creating projects with a computer-guided laser. I’ve done a number of science-themed projects (such as a water bottle covered in the first page of a friend’s publication) and used these as a jumping off point to create the game. Creating the game was a fun way for me to combine my love of microbiology, public health, and creative laser work!



Testing different game board designs with the laser

About Me
Krisandra Allen, MPH, MB(ASCP)CM
I’m an epidemiologist with a background in molecular biology and experience in public health at a local health department, state health department, public health laboratory, and in the private sector. My favorite area of public health practice has always been foodborne and enteric disease, and I have a special place in my heart for norovirus (and once held the official job title of “norovirus epidemiology specialist”). I love bringing together my two areas of experience (lab + epi) to advance the use of genomic epidemiology in public health.
I maintain this site to create a place to pull together resources and materials that can benefit the community. If you have anything you think would be helpful on the site, please reach out with recommendations!

title: Genomic Epidemiology and Public Health
text:
Welcome!
GenomicEpi.com is dedicated to providing resources for the genomic and molecular epidemiology community. You’ll find various pages with information about trainings, graduate programs, and genomic epidemiology jobs.
Please look around, and reach out if there are any resources you think would be helpful that aren’t included.


Public Health | Epidemiology | Molecular Biology
The last decade has brought about incredible advances in sequencing technologies, which have increasingly been leveraged for public health surveillance as well as outbreak detection and investigation. Successfully using genomic data requires a collaborative team and expertise across multiple disciplines including laboratory science, bioinformatics, and epidemiology. It has been exciting to see over the past decade how each of these fields has evolved.
